messages:
julia: hey team, day 1 question — I merged my prod and tools kubeconfigs and now `kubectl get pods -n devops-tools` returns Forbidden for user julia@redwood.com. who owns that namespace?
julia: exact error: `Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User "julia@redwood.com" cannot list resource "pods" in API group "" in the namespace "devops-tools"`
infra: welcome! quick checklist: 1) `kubectl config current-context` 2) `kubectl config view --minify` 3) `kubectl auth can-i list pods --namespace=devops-tools` — paste outputs (no kubeconfigs or tokens)
julia: current-context -> prod-julia
julia: `kubectl auth can-i list pods --namespace=devops-tools` -> no
infra: looks like your default context is still prod — that's the usual pitfall when merging. devops-tools is owned by eng-platform, they grant access via SSO group `eng-platform-devs`. did your Okta groups sync?
julia: not sure, just joined yesterday so maybe not yet. my SSO id is julia@redwood.com, github: juliat
nish: i can create a namespace-scoped RoleBinding for onboarding. i prefer not to give cluster-wide roles. i'll make a 6h `view` binding so you can complete setup and tests.
nish: ran:
```
kubectl create rolebinding onb-julia-devops-tools -n devops-tools --clusterrole=view --user=julia@redwood.com --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```
nish: applied. retry `kubectl get pods -n devops-tools` now.
onboard-bot: Onboarding tip: follow the kube-access guide for persistent access -> https://internal.redwood/docs/onboard/kube-access (requests map your SSO groups automatically).
julia: retried — pods are visible now, thanks :tada: 
julia: couple of follow-ups: 1) how can I avoid the merged-config trap? 2) any quick alias for context switching?
infra: avoid merging prod into your default `~/.kube/config`. keep separate files like `~/.kube/prod` and `~/.kube/dev` and only export `KUBECONFIG` when you need both. alternatives: `kubectx`/`kubens` or explicit context flags.
infra: alias examples we use:
```
# switch context
kubectl config use-context <name>
# helper to run with explicit context
kc() { kubectl --context="$1" "${@:2}"; }
# quick: kc staging get pods -n my-ns
```
infra: also set namespace on context so plain `kubectl get pods` defaults to the right ns:
```
kubectl config set-context dev-julia --namespace=devops-tools --cluster=dev --user=julia@redwood.com
kubectl config use-context dev-julia
```
infra: extra safety: add your current context to PS1 or use a pre-command git/hook that prints `kubectl config current-context` before each kubectl.
nish: note: temporary RoleBindings are audited and expire. open infra access form if you need persistent team access: https://internal.redwood/infra/access — include your team and reason.
julia: perfect — added to my checklist and updated my shell prompt. thanks everyone!
